raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Add an opt-in eager/CUDA Graph measurement objective to the managed FlashInfer autotune warmup. **Stacked on #55671**; review the [isolated follow-up delta](https://github.com/YangXu1990uiuc/vllm/compare/1fee4445c1167e0d7c9bcd2f9cb6d25e1b75afcd...1dcfdf806392ea2795a9a082ae0dc6750ef0bc08). The cache migration can land independently.

## Claims

- `KernelConfig.flashinfer_autotune_execution_mode` accepts `auto` (existing per-op defaults), `eager` (include recurring host cost), and `cuda_graph` (measure captured replay).
- Forward the explicit public `MeasurementPolicy` through generic and sparse-MLA warmup; reject explicit modes when autotuning is disabled or the managed-cache deployment is ineligible.
- Keep the parent's single-rank gate and existing default measurement policy. FlashInfer separates explicit policies into distinct cache namespaces; serving reuses the attached store without a new per-token dispatch or synchronization step.

This is one objective for the whole warmup, **not automatic per-path policy selection**. It does not change vLLM's graph configuration.

## Validation

Source: `1dcfdf806392`; baseline: parent `1fee4445c116`. B200 + Xeon Platinum 8570 (16 allocated CPUs, OMP=4), Qwen3-8B-FP8, MRv2, TP1, Torch 2.13.0, FlashInfer Python/cubin `0.7.0.post1` and JIT cache `0.7.0.post1+cu130`; CUDA runtime 13.0, cuBLAS 13.1.1, cuDNN 9.20 and cuDNN Frontend 1.31.0. Complete Python source overlaid on compatible native wheel `187a0eb98aa4`; no native rebuild. `VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error` was enabled.

- **137 tests passed**: 135 existing warmup/lifecycle tests plus 2 configuration-rejection cases. Existing Model Executor and engine CI suites cover these files.
- **16/16 GPU cases passed**: cold/warm for all four engine/policy combinations, plus two additional independent cold-tuning rounds. Each case verified its policy namespace, serving/capture cache hits, finite selected-token logprobs and actual engine execution mode. All four warm stores remained unchanged with no new profiling calls for this model.
- Formatting and Python 3.12 typing passed. The parent's pre-existing Python 3.11 parse failure in `sharded_state_loader.py:214` is already fixed on main; the standard 3.11 mypy hook also passed with only that upstream syntax fix temporarily overlaid.

Initial hosted CI is **gated**, not green: [pre-run-check](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/actions/runs/38389349806/job/115270912816) reports no qualifying readiness/verification label and 0 qualifying merged PRs for the author. [Read the Docs #35115277](https://app.readthedocs.org/projects/vllm/builds/35115277/) exited in `docs/pre_run_check.sh` because that check did not pass, before building the docs. DCO passed; the local and GPU results above are separate evidence.

**Fixed-token offline `LLM.generate` wall time**: one untimed warmup plus five measurements per workload in each of three independently tuned processes. Table uses the median of per-process medians; speedup is the median paired ratio, with the range across the three tuning rounds. Configuration order alternates between rounds; audit hooks are removed before timing. Baseline uses `auto`; candidate uses the explicit policy matching the named experiment. These are not HTTP serving or TTFT/ITL results.

| Engine configuration | Batch / input / output tokens | Default objective | Explicit objective | Speedup, median (range) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| eager | 1 / 32 / 128 | 7.392 s | 6.560 s | 1.129x (0.997–1.129) |
| eager | 8 / 32 / 128 | 7.880 s | 5.655 s | 1.391x (1.322–1.394) |
| eager | 16 / 1024 / 128 | 8.225 s | 7.468 s | 1.101x (1.041–1.198) |
| graph | 1 / 32 / 128 | 0.377 s | 0.368 s | 1.019x (0.979–1.036) |
| graph | 8 / 32 / 128 | 0.424 s | 0.448 s | 0.947x (0.912–0.970) |
| graph | 16 / 1024 / 128 | 1.991 s | 2.099 s | 0.949x (0.897–0.963) |

`graph` requested `FULL`, but the FlashInfer attention backend resolved it to **FULL_AND_PIECEWISE**. Worker audit observed both full and piecewise replay, plus managed hits during capture. The tested capture sizes were `[1, 2, 4, 8, 16]`; larger/out-of-range prefill runs eagerly. This is a mixed engine with a single global graph measurement objective, not proof of optimal policy selection for every runtime path.

Full GSM8K: 1319 questions, 5-shot, 256-token limit, one evaluation pair per engine configuration. Intervals below are approximate paired normal 95% intervals; these runs do not establish accuracy equivalence.

| Engine | Default objective | Explicit objective | Difference and interval |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| eager | 1149/1319 (87.11%) | 1153/1319 (87.41%) | +0.30 pp; [-1.06, +1.67] |
| graph | 1156/1319 (87.64%) | 1144/1319 (86.73%) | -0.91 pp; [-2.27, +0.45] |

<details>
<summary>Reproduction and local checks</summary>

```bash
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py -q
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest \
  tests/test_config.py -k flashinfer_measurement_requires_autotuning -q
```

Run changed-file pre-commit and `tools/pre_commit/mypy.py 3.12` on the changed Python files. For the 3.11 check on this old stacked base, apply main's existing `sharded_state_loader.py` syntax fix first; it is not part of this feature's delta.

For GPU reproduction, use the versions above and `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 VLLM_GPU_SYNC_CHECK=error OMP_NUM_THREADS=4`. Use a fresh `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_CACHE_DIR` per tuning round, reusing it for the warm restart. Set `enable_prefix_caching=False`, `max_model_len=4096`, `max_num_batched_tokens=512`, `max_num_seqs=16`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.7`, and `seed=0`. Pin `nvidia/Qwen3-8B-FP8` at revision `2cebc4c89e25abc17668c81b01dceaf3d8b914d5`.

Use `enforce_eager=True` for the eager experiments. For graph-enabled experiments, set `compilation_config={"cudagraph_mode": "FULL", "cudagraph_capture_sizes": [1,2,4,8,16]}`. Enable autotuning in `kernel_config`; omit the new field for the baseline and set it to `eager` or `cuda_graph` for the candidate.

For each table row, submit `batch` prompts whose token IDs are `[1000 + i] * input_tokens`, with `SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=128, ignore_eos=True, seed=0)`. Warm once, then time five `LLM.generate(..., use_tqdm=False)` calls and assert exactly `batch * 128` output tokens each. Repeat with three fresh tuning roots, reversing configuration order for the middle round.

Evaluate with `tests.evals.gsm8k.gsm8k_eval._build_gsm8k_prompts(1319, 5)` and `SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=256, seed=42, stop=["Question", "Assistant:", "<|separator|>"])`, then the suite's `_score_gsm8k`.

Example user configuration:

```bash
vllm serve <model> --enforce-eager \
  --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune": true, "flashinfer_autotune_execution_mode": "eager"}'
```

</details>

## Details

Kept as a follow-up because a graph-enabled vLLM engine can mix full graphs, piecewise graphs and eager fallbacks. The knob allows controlled evaluation, but automatically choosing policies also requires matching the winner store to capture and uncaptured execution. Defaults therefore remain unchanged. The configuration field participates in vLLM's kernel hash as well as the explicit policy being part of FlashInfer's managed namespace.

New-policy GPU coverage is limited to this dense FP8 model on B200. SM120 sparse-MLA and MoE need hardware/model coverage; their warmup forwarding and rejection contracts are unit-tested only. Multi-rank managed tuning remains disabled and does not depend on FlashInfer #6185 for this scope. Broader accuracy and runtime-path qualification remain before changing defaults.

Duplicate checks found no `MeasurementPolicy` integration PR. #59995 concerns MoE search strategy and #59698 cache-only startup; this adds the measurement objective on top of the existing #55671 cache migration. AI assistance was used for implementation, review, validation and this description. Human review of the new code remains required before readiness.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

files.patch:
@@ -24,6 +24,34 @@ Beyond the optimization levels, three mechanisms reduce time-to-first-token on r
 - **Skip memory profiling with `--kv-cache-memory`.** On startup, vLLM logs the exact `--kv-cache-memory` value that reproduces the current allocation. Passing it back on the next boot skips the memory-profiling measurement and the CUDA-graph memory estimation pass. Note that this has performance implications: the KV cache is sized to exactly the given value instead of being measured, so a conservative value caps batch concurrency (and therefore throughput), while an optimistic one fails at allocation time. The value is only valid on the same GPU with the same initial free memory; if a boot OOMs after hardware or co-tenant changes, remove the flag to re-profile.
 - **Serve without CUDA graphs using `--enforce-eager`.** Skips both compilation and CUDA-graph capture for the fastest possible startup, at the cost of steady-state decode performance. Useful for development loops and for measuring how much of a boot is compile/capture.
 
+## FlashInfer Autotune Measurement
+
+Eligible single-rank deployments using the FlashInfer managed autotune cache can
+choose how warmup measures kernel candidates with
+`KernelConfig.flashinfer_autotune_execution_mode`:
+
+- `auto` (default) preserves FlashInfer's per-operation measurement defaults.
+- `eager` includes recurring host overhead when measuring a candidate.
+- `cuda_graph` measures candidate execution through CUDA Graph replay.
+
+For example, an eager deployment can enable matching measurement with:
+
+```bash
+vllm serve <model> --enforce-eager \
+    --kernel-config '{"enable_flashinfer_autotune": true, "flashinfer_autotune_execution_mode": "eager"}'
+```
+
+The objective applies to the entire autotune warmup; it does not change vLLM's
+runtime CUDA Graph configuration. Mixed eager/graph deployments do not yet
+select separate winners for each runtime path. Keep `auto` unless an explicit
+objective has been validated for the deployment. FlashInfer stores each explicit
+policy in a separate cache namespace and reuses that store after warmup.
+
+Explicit modes require autotuning to be enabled and the managed-cache path to be
+eligible. Legacy-cache deployments reject an explicit mode rather than silently
+ignoring it. Model-level performance and accuracy still need validation when
+changing kernel selection.
+
 ## Preemption
 
 Due to the autoregressive nature of transformer architecture, there are times when KV cache space is insufficient to handle all batched requests.

@@ -284,6 +284,8 @@ Certain API request parameters can have a large impact on resource consumption a
 
 To mitigate this, vLLM enforces a configurable upper bound on the `n` parameter via the `VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES` environment variable (default: **16384**). Requests exceeding this limit are rejected before reaching the engine.
 
+FlashInfer SM120 sparse MLA also maintains a separate calibration cache controlled by `FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_DIR`. Managed-cache reload does not synchronize its calibration parameters across ranks. Pre-calibrate on idle, compatible hardware and deploy a consistent calibration artifact when reproducible kernel selection is required.
+
 ### Recommendations
 
 - **Public-facing deployments:** Consider setting `VLLM_MAX_N_SEQUENCES` to a value appropriate for your workload (e.g., `64` or `128`) to limit the blast radius of a single request.

 4. **Stop a managed engine** through `Control.Shutdown`, or cause denial of service by exploiting bugs in the gRPC interface.

+

 - Only enable `--grpc-port` when you have a specific need for gRPC-based inference

 | Environment Variable | Default | Description |
 | --- | --- | --- |
-| `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` | `~/.cache/vllm` | Base cache directory. Respects `XDG_CACHE_HOME` if set. All paths below inherit from this unless explicitly overridden. |
+| `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` | `~/.cache/vllm` | Base directory for vLLM-owned caches. Respects `XDG_CACHE_HOME` if set. |
 | *(torch.compile)* | `$VLLM_CACHE_ROOT/torch_compile_cache/` | Compilation cache for AOT-compiled models, Inductor graphs, and Triton kernels. Controlled by `VLLM_DISABLE_COMPILE_CACHE` (set to `1` to disable). |
-| `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_CACHE_DIR` | `$VLLM_CACHE_ROOT/flashinfer_autotune_cache/<flashinfer-version>/<arch>/<cache-hash>/` | FlashInfer autotune config cache. |
+| `VLLM_FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_CACHE_DIR` | FlashInfer's managed-cache default, or the legacy path described below | Overrides FlashInfer autotune cache placement for both cache APIs. |
 | `VLLM_ASSETS_CACHE` | `$VLLM_CACHE_ROOT/assets/` | Downloaded assets (e.g., tokenizer files). |
 | `VLLM_XLA_CACHE_PATH` | `$VLLM_CACHE_ROOT/xla_cache/` | XLA/TPU compilation cache. |
 | `VLLM_MEDIA_CACHE` | *(disabled)* | Optional cache for downloaded media (images, video, audio). Not enabled unless explicitly set. |
 
+Single-rank deployments with Elastic EP disabled use FlashInfer's managed autotune cache when available. Multi-rank deployments retain legacy cache synchronization until the pinned FlashInfer coordinates cache-hit decisions before profiling. Without a vLLM override, FlashInfer uses `FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_CACHE_DIR`, or its default `~/.cache/flashinfer/autotune` (relocated by `FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BASE`). `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` does not relocate this managed store. Use a separate store root for each independently tuning deployment, including separate prefill and decode instances. Directory sharing alone does not synchronize cache-hit decisions. After interrupted tuning, use a fresh store root when diagnosing incomplete caches.
+
+The legacy fallback retains `$VLLM_CACHE_ROOT/flashinfer_autotune_cache/<flashinfer-version>/<arch>/<cache-hash>/`. Each rank saves its own `autotune_configs_dp<dp>_rank<rank>.json`. With PP>1, each stage's TP group coordinates cache loading and profiling independently.
+
+FlashInfer SM120 sparse MLA also maintains a separate calibration cache controlled by `FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_DIR`. Managed-cache reload does not synchronize its calibration parameters across ranks. Pre-calibrate on idle, compatible hardware and deploy a consistent calibration artifact when reproducible kernel selection is required.
+
 ### Recommendations
 
 - **Restrict file permissions** on `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` (and any other cache directories used by dependencies, such as `~/.triton` if compile caching is disabled) so that only the vLLM process owner can read and write to them.
@@ -608,6 +618,8 @@ Scope the salt to the isolation boundary you need:
 - **Per-group sharing**: A shared random salt for users who are allowed to benefit from each other's cached prefixes, such as users within the same organization.
 - **No salt**: Omitting `cache_salt` preserves the default behavior where all requests can share cached prefixes. This is appropriate for single-tenant deployments or when prefix privacy is not a concern.
 
+FlashInfer SM120 sparse MLA also maintains a separate calibration cache controlled by `FLASHINFER_AUTOTUNE_DIR`. Managed-cache reload does not synchronize its calibration parameters across ranks. Pre-calibrate on idle, compatible hardware and deploy a consistent calibration artifact when reproducible kernel selection is required.
+
